newsitem.title: USA: Cinergy sets service to TVA customer.
newsitem.headline: Cinergy sets service to TVA customer.

text.p: Cinergy Corp said it has tentatively agreed to providce the Bristol, Va., municipal electric system's power requirements for a seven-year period beginning January 1, 1988.

Bristol, located in southwest Virginia, has native load requirements and is now a wholesale customer of the Tennessee Valley Authority Cinergy said it expects a supply contract based on the memorandum of understanding reached with Bristol to be completed by February 13.
One Cinergy spokesman said "This marks the first time any of the 160 distributors of electricty in the seven states associated with the Tennessee Valley Authority have dropped TVA as a supplier."
Cinergy said it was chosen from 19 suppliers that submitted bids to Bristol.

Spokesman Steve Brash said Bristol expects "considerable savings" under the agreement, adding it is looking into invsting this in a second interconnection, probably with the American Electric Power Co Inc system.
Cinergy will wheel power to Bristol through its interconnect with TVA, he noted.
Brash declined to discuss power prices under the contract, saying Cinergy was chosen, at least in part, for the ancillary services it is offering, including help with new business development.

In its statement, the utility said the agreement also provides for the potential of retail customer choice, allowing the town to reduce purchases during the contract without penalty if the utility does not reduce its price to allow Bristol to retain customer load.
